B: Hi! Right, here we go. Nicola.
A: Hello. I'm Denise. Sorry, I've just moved the laptop, is that better?
B: Yeah, you're fine. Where are you?
A: St Helens. Near Liverpool, sort of.
B: Oh right. I'm Woodley, near Reading. What do you do, Denise?
A: I'm a dental technician. I make crowns and bridges for the dentists, in a little lab in town.
B: Oh, interesting. Do you get paid decent for that? Sorry, that's me, I always ask about money.
A: Erm, it's alright. It's not a fortune. I've been there twenty-five years, so it's steady. I'm just worried one of the big chains'll buy us out.
B: Yeah, that's what happens, isn't it. Everything gets bought up. I'm a consultant, SAP, finance systems, so I'm usually the one they bring in after the big chain's bought everyone. Sort of the other side of it.
A: Oh. I don't really know what that is, sorry.
B: Nobody does. Basically I move company accounts onto new software and make it work. Long hours, decent day rate. I'm on a contract in Bracknell and the traffic on the A329 is killing me.
A: I couldn't do all that driving. I walk to work.
B: Lucky you. Got family round you?
A: My mum, about ten minutes away. I go round most days. She's eighty-one. My brother's in Devon, so it's mostly me.
B: Yeah. My dad's starting to go a bit, health-wise. My sister's nearer him, so she does most of it, if I'm honest.
A: It's a lot, isn't it. Is he alright?
B: He's, you know. Up and down. She rings me with updates and I feel a bit useless, sat in a meeting in Bracknell. So, yeah.
A: I'm sure she knows you'd help if you could.
B: Maybe. Anyway. What do you do for fun, then?
A: Oh, not much. I walk by the canal, I do jigsaws, I bake for church. I've got a harbour one on the go, a thousand pieces. I'm stuck on the sky.
B: A thousand pieces? I'd lose patience after ten. I play padel, that's my thing. It's like tennis but smaller.
A: I think I've seen that on the telly. Is it hard?
B: Not really, it's just fast. You'd probably be alright, you've got steady hands.
A: Ha, I don't know about that. I'd be no good running about. I do an aqua class on a Wednesday, that's my lot.
B: That counts. Do you go away much?
A: North Wales, or the Lakes, most years. I'm not keen on flying. I went on a coach to Austria once with church, that was nice.
B: Oh, I'm the opposite, get me on a plane. Mauritius last year, all-inclusive. You'd love it, honestly, you just lie there.
A: I think I'd worry the whole flight. Sorry, is that what you wanted? I'm not very interesting.
B: No, you're fine. What's for your dinner tonight, then?
A: My tea? Scouse, probably. I made a big pan on Sunday.
